title: Marketplace shared vocabulary
description: ONE physical definition per constraint (config-first P-1, adopted via TOURNAMENT-VERDICT.md M6). Every other marketplace schema $refs these $defs instead of re-declaring a pattern. A second copy of `sha256` would be a second control plane.

sha256.description: Prefixed lowercase hex digest. The prefix is mandatory so an unprefixed hex string can never be silently accepted as a digest of a different algorithm.

version_range.description: Deliberately small range grammar: exact, comparator, caret, tilde, or `*`. A grammar nobody can enumerate is a grammar nobody can gate.

channel.description: Closed set. An unknown channel string must fail validation rather than resolve to a default; `mkt.index` never falls back.

spdx.description: SPDX identifier or a simple compound expression. NOT a licence-validity claim -- the LICENCE POLICY in trust-policy.schema.json decides acceptability.

permission.description: `<capability>:<scope>`. The capability half is a CLOSED set so a novel capability cannot be smuggled in as free text; the scope half is open but `*` is what the trust policy scores as excessive.

relative_path.description: Payload paths are relative, forward-slash, and may not traverse. The char class is a POSITIVE allowlist, so backslash, colon and whitespace are rejected by construction -- a Windows-style payload path is how a containment check gets bypassed on one platform and not the other.

score_0_100.description: INTEGER, not number. The canonical JSON form used for digests and signatures forbids floats outright (mkt.canon), so a float score could not be signed deterministically.
